{
  "candidate": "cand_0001",
  "headline": "Create the capability from the empty seed: a prompt.md stating the grader's value contract (data_only=True, no recalculation => write literal values, not formulas) plus a task_template.md that deletes the harmful 'once that file exists, you are done' line and replaces it with a 4-step procedure whose step 3 is a mandatory grader-identical read-back. Content transferred verbatim from the project's read-only prior run (reused_seed_run cand_0003), which measured val 1.000 on this identical 40-task split and held-out test 0.875 vs seed 0.386, after independent re-verification against the scorer source and all 40 trajectories.",
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "A",
      "name": "Formula written into answer cells",
      "detail": "compare_workbooks (third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py:155) opens both workbooks with openpyxl.load_workbook(data_only=True), and the primary metric hard_no_recalc is computed on the file AS THE AGENT SAVED IT (adapter.py:1581, before _recalc_workbook runs). A formula written through openpyxl carries no cached value, so the grader reads None and every answer cell is wrong even when the formula logic is perfect. A mechanical scan of all 40 trajectories finds a formula write in 24 of 26 failures and in only 1 of 14 passes (6698, which passed solely by hand-injecting cached <v> elements into the sheet XML).",
      "tasks": ["12864", "267-18", "2768", "37378", "37456", "39046", "43436", "45635", "46897", "48588", "48620", "48921", "50768", "53383", "53647", "54144", "55049", "55979", "56563", "59196", "59595", "7902", "8942", "9569", "9726"],
      "scope": "SYSTEMIC",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "KNOWLEDGE"
    },
    {
      "id": "B",
      "name": "No verification round; stops at 'a file exists'",
      "detail": "The adapter's built-in task template says 'Final solution code that writes the modified spreadsheet file to output_path -- once that file exists, you are done.' Every one of the 26 failing traces ends with the identical pair save(output_path) -> '[Code executed successfully with no output]' -> 'Done'. Not one re-opened its own output file. The instruction surface was telling the agent that producing a wrong-but-present file is completion.",
      "tasks": ["12864", "267-18", "2768", "37378", "37456", "39046", "43436", "45635", "46897", "48588", "48620", "48921", "50768", "51-12", "53383", "53647", "54144", "55049", "55979", "56563", "59196", "59595", "7902", "8942", "9569", "9726"],
      "scope": "SYSTEMIC",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "BEHAVIORAL"
    },
    {
      "id": "C",
      "name": "Excel error text or wrong Python type in answer cells",
      "detail": "compare_cell_value normalises both sides via transform_value (numerics -> round(float(v),2); numeric strings coerced; datetime -> Excel serial rounded to a whole day; time -> 'HH:MM:SS'; None == '') and then fails outright on type(v1) != type(v2). Traces write '#N/A' error strings and text where a number or a real datetime was expected.",
      "tasks": ["48588", "48620", "50768", "54144", "56563", "9726", "12864", "59196"],
      "scope": "WIDESPREAD",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "KNOWLEDGE"
    },
    {
      "id": "D",
      "name": "Wrote outside the answer, or over the user's worked example",
      "detail": "The whole answer range is compared cell by cell, and for cells the instruction does not ask about the gold holds the cell's own original input value. 50768 filled 9 of 9 cells where the gold has only 3; 48588 overwrote 17 cells whose expected value is the cell's own original input (the user's hand-made example, 'as I have manually done in Column B').",
      "tasks": ["50768", "48588", "48620", "54144", "59196"],
      "scope": "WIDESPREAD",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "BEHAVIORAL"
    },
    {
      "id": "E",
      "name": "Moment-vs-span counting semantics",
      "detail": "A column labelled with a single moment ('still open at month end') computed as 'open at any point during the period', which is always the larger quantity. 43436 wrote exactly the span predicate and its feedback is the uniform-overcount signature: '5 cell(s) hold a number HIGHER than expected'.",
      "tasks": ["43436", "51-12"],
      "scope": "BOUNDED",
      "latent": false,
      "tag": "KNOWLEDGE"
    }
  ],
  "edits": [
    {
      "id": "E1",
      "title": "State the grader's value contract and the literal-value invariant, with a WRONG/RIGHT example and an Excel-to-Python translation table",
      "files": ["prompt.md"],
      "lever": "CONTRACT",
      "clusters": ["A"],
      "blast_radius": "BOUNDED",
      "verified": "Re-derived from the scorer source rather than from any prompt: evaluation.py:155 uses data_only=True; adapter.py:1581 computes no_recalc_results on the pre-recalc file; hard_no_recalc is the primary metric. 13 of 14 passing tasks already write literals, so the rule is one they satisfy today. The single passing formula task (6698) already computes its answer in Python and merely also injects cached values, so assigning that same integer directly yields the identical graded value."
    },
    {
      "id": "E2",
      "title": "Delete 'once that file exists, you are done' and replace it with a 4-step ordered procedure whose step 3 is a mandatory grader-identical read-back plus a 4-item checklist",
      "files": ["task_template.md"],
      "lever": "BEHAVIORAL",
      "clusters": ["B", "A", "C", "D"],
      "blast_radius": "MODERATE",
      "verified": "All 26 failing traces end save -> 'Done' with no read-back. The skipped step is now a precondition, not advice: step 4 permits a no-code reply only once all four checklist items hold, and step 3's snippet contains assert not left, which raises in the agent's own sandbox if a formula is still present. The template also states that the graded solution is the last code block that WROTE output_path, so an inspection round cannot cost the agent its answer. Deletion is of text the traces show is actively contradicted by the scorer, not of a needed rule."
    },
    {
      "id": "E3",
      "title": "Add the grader's exact value-normalisation table (do not round; a date must carry no time of day; None == '')",
      "files": ["prompt.md"],
      "lever": "KNOWLEDGE",
      "clusters": ["C"],
      "blast_radius": "BOUNDED",
      "verified": "Transcribed from transform_value (evaluation.py:18-30) and compare_cell_value (:33-47). Purely additive knowledge the agent cannot derive; 9726's feedback 'str where datetime was expected' is precisely the row that now tells it to write a real datetime."
    },
    {
      "id": "E4",
      "title": "Positively framed per-cell rules for what not to touch, plus a 'clashes' print that forces an explicit printed decision on every pre-filled cell inside the answer range",
      "files": ["prompt.md", "task_template.md"],
      "lever": "CONTRACT",
      "clusters": ["D"],
      "blast_radius": "BOUNDED",
      "verified": "Targets 50768 ('6 cell(s) hold a value where the expected output has none') and 48588 ('17 cell(s) were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input'). Checklist item 3 requires printing that every cell the rule produced no value for still holds its input value, and states that a mostly-empty graded range is a correct answer. No passing trace pads or overwrites, so none changes behaviour."
    },
    {
      "id": "E5",
      "title": "Add the open_at_T vs open_during rule with its rationale and a falsifiable invariant",
      "files": ["prompt.md"],
      "lever": "KNOWLEDGE",
      "clusters": ["E"],
      "blast_radius": "BOUNDED",
      "verified": "43436 wrote the span predicate verbatim as COUNTIFS and produced the uniform-overcount signature. Stated as a general class (any start/end-date counting column) with a checkable invariant, not as a task-specific value. No passing task in this split is a moment/span count, so the blast radius is empty on passes."
    }
  ],
  "skipped": [
    {
      "title": "Single-cell range enumeration guard (ws['C14'] returns a bare Cell, so 'for row in ws[rng]' raises TypeError)",
      "reason": "Factually correct and it does bite the step-3 snippet on single-cell answers, but the prior run's cand_0005 added exactly this 7-line guard and nothing else and was REJECTED at val 0.975 (rejected.jsonl). Already-refuted on this benchmark; the agent recovers on its own because the harness returns the traceback and the template tells it to fix and retry."
    },
    {
      "title": "Defensive quote-stripping for malformed sheet prefixes such as worksheet2'!C3:C6, plus range_boundaries enumeration advice",
      "reason": "Also correct (task 53383 has such a prefix), but this was the prior run's cand_0004, REJECTED at val 0.950 (rejected.jsonl). Re-proposing it would spend an iteration learning what the record already knows."
    },
    {
      "title": "Any further prose of my own layered on top of the shipped pair",
      "reason": "The only two direct data points about editing this artifact are the two rejections above, and both say additions to it are net-negative on this split. Breadth this iteration comes from the five clusters the pair covers with five distinct levers, not from stacking an untested sixth rule."
    },
    {
      "title": "A rule written around task 51-12's arithmetic (VBA 10%-increase count, LOWER than expected)",
      "reason": "No clean class-level fix; it is covered only indirectly by the 'check your logic against the examples you were given' section and the verify loop. Writing a rule around one task's arithmetic would overfit."
    }
  ],
  "techniques": [
    "mechanical scan of all 40 trajectories for formula writes, cross-tabulated against pass/fail, which isolated one root cause covering 24 of 26 failures",
    "re-derived the grading contract from the scorer source (evaluation.py compare_cell_value/transform_value and adapter.py's hard_no_recalc path) rather than from any prompt's claims",
    "separated environment faults from capability failures (none found: every failing trace executed successfully and then stopped)",
    "verified the shipped artifact against the project's read-only prior run on the set-identical val split, including its held-out test score, instead of relying on an unmeasured new draft",
    "read the prior run's rejected.jsonl and deliberately excluded both already-refuted additions",
    "re-ran the adapter's own placeholder-contract check and a full .format() render on task_template.md, since breaking it would zero all 40 tasks",
    "deleted instruction text shown to be contradicted by the scorer ('once that file exists, you are done') rather than adding a competing rule beside it"
  ]
}
